name: pull-request-reviews
title: Pull request reviews
description: A code and security review of every pull request as project code: a review chat per pull request on a review pool that verifies the change by running it, and a workflow that posts the review, a check run and a summary to GitHub.
docs:
Install into a project attached to its GitHub repository, on a Work server with the company's GitHub App connected; the Work server guide's "Review pull requests with Work" covers the server side (the App and its webhook, the service connections, the review machines).

1. Copy the files to their targets, merging rather than overwriting: add the manifest's `review` and `github-poster` Environments to the project's `.work/project.json` and keep its other Environments, and keep an existing `.work/triggers/github.ts` that already matches. Drop the `prod` and `slack` bindings the organization has not set up; the reviewer treats both as optional.
2. In `.work/workflows/src/reviews.ts`, replace `acme/web` (every trigger's `where`, and `REVIEWED_REPOSITORY`) with the project's repository as `owner/name`: the App's webhook delivers every repository it is installed on.
3. Map GitHub logins to project members in `GITHUB_MEMBERS`, or commit a `reviewers` role: they approve the chat's escalations.
4. Make `review` fit the repository: its `setup.command` installs the change's dependencies (list every host it reaches in `setup.network.allow`), and the image needs the repository's toolchains.
5. Check the project (`program_check`), deploy, and turn the workflows on as the installed `.work/skills/pull-request-reviews/SKILL.md` says ("Turn it on and check it"). That skill stays with the project and explains each file.

For a reviewer on an open-weight model, add the `pull-request-reviews-opencode` pack after this one.
